editorial: When a secluded Montana house becomes the stage for a quiet psychological unraveling, you sense the tension rising before it even unfurls. The film, a slow‑burn psychological drama, digs into the fragile edges of love and motherhood with a rural setting that feels both blanketed and suffocating. The most arresting element is the extended, dead‑pan night vision sequence, a stunning montage that turns the inside of the house into a labyrinth of unsaid fears. A slight slowdown in the middle act stretches the narrative, giving some scenes an uneven cadence. You’ll find it compelling if you thrive on intimate, character‑driven stories that slowly peel back the layers of identity.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
